.
This holy Archangel identified himself to the exiled Jew Tobias as one of the Seven who stand before God(Tob. 12:15). His name means the healing of God, and he is thought to be the Angel who came down and agitated the water of the pool of Bethsaida in Jerusalem. The sick, who always lay around the pool, strove to be the first to enter the water afterwards, because that fortunate one was always cured. We read of this in the story of the paralytic cured by Jesus, who had waited patiently for thirty-eight years, unable to move when the occasion presented itself. (Cf. John 5:1-9)
.
Saint Raphael is best known through the beautiful history of the two Tobias, father and son, exiled to Persia in the days of the Assyrian conquest in the eighth century before Christ. In their story, the Archangel plays the major role.
.
The father Tobias was a faithful son of Jacob and was old and worn out by his manifold good works; for many years he had assisted his fellow exiles in every possible way, even burying the slain of Israel during a persecution by Sennacherib, and continuing this practice despite the wrath that king manifested towards him. Having been stripped of all his possessions, he desired to have his son recover a substantial sum of money he had once lent to a member of his family in a distant city. He needed a companion for the young Tobias. God provided that guide in the Archangel Raphael, whom the son met providentially one day, in the person of a stranger from the very area where he was to go, in the country of the Medes. Raphael to all appearances was a young man like himself, who said his name was Azarias (Assistance of God).Everything went well, as proposed; the young Tobias recovered the sum and then was married, during their stay in Media, to the virtuous daughter of another relative, whom Providence had reserved for him.
.
All aspects of this journey had been thorny with difficulties, but the wise guide had found a way to overcome all of them. When a huge fish threatened to devour Tobias, camped on the shores of the Tigris, the guide told him how to remove it from the water, and the fish expired at his feet; then remedies and provisions were derived from this creature by the directives of Azarias. When the Angel led Tobias for lodging in the city of Rages, to the house of his kinsman Raguel, father of the beautiful Sara, the young man learned that seven proposed husbands had died on the very day of the planned marriage. How would Tobias fare? The Angel reassured him that this would not be his own fate, and told him to pray with his future spouse for three nights, that they might be blessed with a holy posterity. Sara was an only daughter, as Tobias was an only son, and she was endowed with a large heritage.
.
During the absence of the young Tobias, his father had become blind when the droppings of a pigeon had fallen into his eyes. When the two travelers returned after an extended absence, which had cost his mother many tears, the young Tobias was deeply grieved to find his father unable to see him and his new daughter-in-law. But Raphael told the son how to cure his father's blindness by means of the gall of the fish; and after the remedy had proved efficacious, all of them rejoiced time in their blessings.
.
When Tobias the son narrated his story and told his father that all their benefits had come to them through this stranger, both father and son wished to give Azarias half of the inheritance. Raphael declined and revealed his identity, saying he was sent to assist the family of the man who had never failed to obey and honor the blessed God of Israel. Raphael, before he disappeared, said to the family: It is honorable to reveal and confess the works of God. Prayer is good, with fasting and alms, more than to lay up treasures, for alms deliver from death and purge away sins, and cause the giver to find mercy and life everlasting... When thou didst pray with tears and didst bury the dead, and didst leave thy dinner to hide the dead by day in thy house, and bury them by night, I offered thy prayer to the Lord. And because thou wast acceptable to God, it was necessary that trials prove thee... I am the Angel Raphael, one of the seven who stand before the Lord.
.
Eternal Father, I wish to honor St. Raphael the Archangel, and I give Thee thanks for all the graces Thou hast bestowed upon him. I ask Thee to please increase grace in my soul through the merits of this saint, and I commit the end of my life to him by this special prayer, so that by virtue of Thy goodness and promise, St. Raphael the Archangel might be my advocate and provide whatever is needed at that hour. Amen.

text:
The Car Dealership Tried to Sneak $5,384 in Extras Into My Loan…Then Accused Me of Lying

I went to an Ohio Honda dealership to buy my first car. I left with a new CR-V, thousands of dollars in charges I never agreed to, and a dealership that suddenly couldn’t answer my calls.

While waiting for the business manager, I sat at my salesman’s desk with my boyfriend. The manager came over and said he was waiting for the banks to respond.

A little later, he returned with the news that I was approved.

But there was a catch.

He claimed one bank would offer a certain interest rate only if I purchased what he called a “bumper-to-bumper warranty.” When my boyfriend questioned him, the manager pushed back and refused to show us the numbers without the warranty.

He made it sound like questioning the deal would somehow create problems with the bank.

I was buying my first car, so I didn’t know what was normal. But something about the conversation didn’t sit right with me.

text:
Super Grok: Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign (and aligned groups) introduced and weaponized it as a campaign attack; Amy Acton had already disclosed the history publicly years earlier.**

Amy Acton first publicly described her childhood sexual abuse in a 2019 *Youngstown Vindicator* profile, long before the 2026 governor’s race. She recounted being molested by her mother’s husband (stepfather Cledith Arthur) between roughly ages 9–12, periods of neglect and instability (including living in a tent one winter), removal from her mother’s custody after authorities intervened, and permanent estrangement from her mother after 1978 court proceedings. Court records and contemporaneous reporting confirm that Arthur was arrested, charged, and indicted by a grand jury in 1978 for raping then-12-year-old Acton; he later failed to appear and became a fugitive. Acton’s brother Philip Stearns has corroborated the account. Acton has referenced the difficult childhood (abuse, neglect, instability) as part of her biography during her time as Ohio health director and in the campaign.

Ramaswamy’s side made it a campaign issue:
- In April 2026, Ramaswamy posted a video saying Acton offered no positive vision “other than to complain about what someone else did to her,” a remark widely read as dismissing her abuse history.
- A Ramaswamy-aligned super PAC (V-PAC) ran ads highlighting Acton’s 1994 medical licensure disclosure that she sought therapy related to childhood sexual abuse.
- In October 2026, Ramaswamy’s campaign produced and confirmed an ad featuring her estranged birth mother, Donna Arthur (who has not spoken to Acton since the 1978 proceedings and stayed with the stepfather). In the ad, Arthur calls Acton a liar about her past (including the tent/homelessness claim) and says she has “a serious problem” and “needs help.” The campaign said it would spend $4 million airing it. The ad does not explicitly detail the sexual abuse, but by platforming the mother who sided with the accused stepfather and disputing Acton’s childhood narrative, it forced the abuse history into the center of the race. Acton, her brother, and others accused Ramaswamy of turning the sexual abuse into a political talking point. Ramaswamy defended the ad as a legitimate credibility attack.

In short, Acton disclosed the facts of her childhood long before the campaign. Ramaswamy’s campaign is the one that brought the estranged mother into the race and aggressively attacked Acton over her accounts of that childhood.

text:
CREDIBLE BUT NOT PUBLICLY PROVEN

The identities and locations of the alleged advanced Iranian plots.

Whether the plans involve direct IRGC operators, Hezbollah, criminal intermediaries or locally recruited facilitators.

That every Houthi-claimed Saudi target was engaged or damaged.

Houthi claims that Saudi officers were overseeing mobilisation at the struck Al-Nasr camp in Aden.

The existence of a final US–Israeli decision authorising renewed attacks on Iran.

Operational Iranian direction of European street disorder.

Direct Chinese or Russian provision of current targeting data.

Implementation of Iran’s reported plans to attack Gulf communications cables.

The complete alleged Fairford plot and the responsibility of individual defendants, which remain matters for active legal proceedings.

Proxy wind up to forward mounting in Mexico and Colombia. 

ANALYTICAL JUDGEMENT

The DNI warning should produce targeted protection, not a uniform global threat declaration.

The highest-risk locations are those combining strategic relevance with demonstrated access: Gulf and Levant missions, airbases, logistics hubs, port visits, predictable transport, contractors, senior officials and institutions already subjected to surveillance.

Europe faces a broader but case-specific hybrid threat. Fairford and previous investigations justify scrutiny of covert facilitation. They do not establish that every protest, arson attack, criminal act or pro-Palestinian mobilisation is Iranian-directed.

THE PRINCIPAL BOXES

BOX ONE
THE OVERSEAS PLOT

Selected by Iran: threaten or attack Americans through dispersed, deniable networks.

Why selected: the United States can defend a carrier group more easily than every diplomat, former official, contractor, family movement and temporary hotel.

What Tehran believes is inside: deterrence through uncertainty, reduced US presence and leverage against renewed strikes.

What may actually be inside: arrests, financial exposure, allied intelligence mobilisation and a retaliation coalition much broader than the one confronting Iran today.

Beneficiary: Iran if disruption remains deniable and non-lethal.

Critical failure: an attributable mass-casualty attack.

Escalation pathway: disrupted or completed plot → public attribution → sanctions and arrests → US or allied kinetic retaliation → Iranian proxy activation.

BOX TWO 
“ANOTHER LITTLE EPIC FURY”

Selected by Washington: a short strike restoring deterrence without entering another open-ended war.

Why selected: sanctions and maritime pressure have not produced Iranian capitulation, while visible force offers political clarity.

Expected contents: destroyed launchers, naval assets, nuclear infrastructure or command nodes followed by negotiations.

Possible actual contents: overseas attacks, Houthi escalation, cable disruption, attacks on Gulf installations and demands from Israel to enlarge the target list.

The central deception is the adjective “little.” Washington chooses the opening attack; Tehran and its partners help determine the size of the war that follows.

BOX THREE
THE GULF EXCLUSION ZONE

Selected by Iran: declare that US warships will not be permitted inside the Persian Gulf.

Why selected: Iran wants to transform geography into deterrence and force Washington to choose between accepting restriction and risking an incident.

Expected contents: greater Iranian control of Hormuz and increased Gulf pressure on Washington.

Possible actual contents: US freedom-of-navigation operations, UAS harassment, warning shots, mines or an attempted interdiction escalating into direct combat.

Iran gains while the warning remains psychological. It loses if an unsuccessful challenge exposes limits or unifies Gulf governments behind a permanent US naval presence.

text: A mandate is not a choice, and that distinction is the whole problem. If a business wants to offer a 32-hour week, the market already allows it, and workers are free to choose employers who do. But writing it into law forces every employer, including small firms running on thin margins, to pay 40 hours of wages for 32 hours of work. That is a 25% jump in hourly labor cost overnight, imposed by decree rather than earned by productivity. The predictable result is fewer hires, shorter shifts for hourly workers, higher prices for customers, or automation replacing the very jobs the law claims to protect. Productivity gains should be shared through competition and growth, not dictated from Washington. Workers deserve higher pay because their work is worth more, not because Congress redefined the week. A free labor market beats a one-size-fits-all mandate every time.

Although this hypothesis can never be proved, it is interesting to note that England, over the next century, rapidly became the dominant power in the old world. The wealth of the Templars could most certainly lie at the heart of what was eventually to become the British Empire.

Another indication that the English may have assisted the Priory of Sion is the fact that the Knights Hospitaller of St. John, or the Hospitallers as they came to be known, acquired the holdings of the Templars after their 1314 persecution. The Hospitallers were the 12th century English competitors of the Knights Templars during the Crusades.58Mter the Saracens regained Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187, one group of Hospitallers landed on the island of Rhodes, changing its name to the Temple of St. John of Jerusalem, and the other landed on the island of Malta, changing its name to the Knights of Malta. British journalist Stephen Knight, author of The Brotherhood (1984), states that both orders are today English Masonic Military Orders.59 Moreover, the authors of The Messianic Legacy state that the Knights of Malta are also today viewed as an ideal conduit for English Masonic intelligence gathering.

A third indication that the British may have assisted the Priory of Sion at La Rochelle is the fact that the Templars fled to Scotland soon after their suppression and there fought alongside King Robert Bruce, who was at war with England. Why would the Templars travel to such a remote place and take arms against England, unless it was related to the disappearance of their galleys at La Rochelle and the confiscation of all their holdings by the English controlled Hospitallers?

Mystery at Rennes-le-Chateau: Grail and Gold 
In the seizure of the Templars, their property and wealth, that Templar stronghold, Rennes-le- Chateau, would not have been overlooked. Hidden in man-made vaults in the hills above the 78 chateau was the Holy Grail and the alleged wealth of Solomon. Investigation into the activities at Rennes-le-Chateau reveal, however, that of all the Templars arrested, those stationed at this small hamlet in southern France went untouched, causing the Holy Blood investigators to suggest that Pope Clement was a double agent, working for the Templars instead of the king. The authors of Holy Blood suggest several reasons: (1) Pope Clement's family was from that area; (2) the Pope still knew many people there, even those guarding the chateau; and (3) history reveals he was slow to prosecute the Templars, although hand-picked by the king to do so.

A slightly different reading of these facts, however, offers a more plausible reason for the protection of Rennes-le-Chateau. Because the Pope was a Merovingian, he would not be likely to protect guards who were Templars. What if the guards were imposters - imposters dressed like Templars, who, perhaps, were Sionist? By the arrangements of the Canadian federation, Canada's monarchy operates in Alberta as the core of the province's Westminster-style parliamentary democracy.[1] As such, the Crown within Alberta's jurisdiction is referred to as the Crown in Right of Alberta,[2] His Majesty in Right of Alberta,[3] or The King in Right of Alberta.[4] The Constitution Act, 1867, however, leaves many royal duties in Alberta specifically assigned to the sovereign's viceroy, the Lieutenant Governor of Alberta,[1] whose direct participation in governance is limited by the conventional stipulations of constitutional monarchy.[5]

Constitutional role
Main article: Monarchy in the Canadian provinces
The role of the Crown is both legal and practical; it functions in Alberta in the same way it does in all of Canada's other provinces, being the centre of a constitutional construct in which the institutions of government acting under the sovereign's authority share the power of the whole.[6] It is thus the foundation of the executive, legislative, and judicial branches of the province's government.[7]

The Canadian monarch—since 8 September 2022, King Charles III—is represented and his duties carried out by the Lieutenant Governor of Alberta, whose direct participation in governance is limited by the conventional stipulations of constitutional monarchy, with most related powers entrusted for exercise by the elected parliamentarians, the ministers of the Crown generally drawn from amongst them, and the judges and justices of the peace.[5] The Crown today primarily functions as a guarantor of continuous and stable governance and a nonpartisan safeguard against the abuse of power.[5][8][9] This arrangement began with the granting of royal assent to the 1905 Alberta Act and continued an unbroken line of monarchical government extending back to the late 18th century.[10] However, though Alberta has a separate government headed by the King, as a province, Alberta is not itself a kingdom.[11]

The Alberta Sovereignty Within a United Canada Act gives the lieutenant governor the unique ability to, following a resolution passed by the legislature, and on ministerial advice, amend any piece of legislation ("Henry VIII powers"),[12] as well as to direct "provincial entities" to disobey any federal law for up to four years.[13] The constitutionality of these powers remains untested.

Government House in Edmonton is owned by the sovereign only in his capacity as King in Right of Alberta and is used both as an office and official event location by the lieutenant governor, the sovereign, and other members of the Canadian royal family. The viceroy resides in a separate home provided by the provincial Crown and the King and his relations reside at a hotel when in Alberta. A member of the royal family have owned Alberta property in a private capacity; King Edward VIII (later the Duke of Windsor) owned the E.P. Ranch (formerly the Bedingfield Ranch), near High River, for more than 40 years.

In the Gospel of Matthew, "μάγοι" (magoi) from the east pay homage to the Christ Child,[1] and the transliterated plural "magi" entered English from Latin in this context around 1200 AD (this particular use is also commonly rendered in English as "kings" and more often in recent times as "wise men").[2] The singular "magus" appears considerably later, when it was borrowed from Old French in the late 14th century with the meaning magician.

Hereditary Zoroastrian priesthood has survived in India[3][4] and Iran. They are termed Herbad, Mobad (Magupat, i.e. chief of the Maga), and Dastur depending on the rank.

History
An unrelated term, but previously assumed to be related, appears in the older Gathic Avestan language texts. This word, adjectival magavan meaning "possessing maga-", was once the premise that Avestan maga- and Median (i.e. Old Persian) magu- were coeval (and also that both these were cognates of Vedic Sanskrit magha-). While "in the Gathas the word seems to mean both the teaching of Zoroaster and the community that accepted that teaching", and it seems that Avestan maga- is related to Sanskrit magha-, "there is no reason to suppose that the western Iranian form magu (Magus) has exactly the same meaning"[8] as well. But it "may be, however", that Avestan moghu (which is not the same as Avestan maga-) "and Medean magu were the same word in origin, a common Iranian term for 'member of the tribe' having developed among the Medes the special sense of 'member of the (priestly) tribe', hence a priest."[6]cf[7]

Some examples of the use of magi in Persian poetry, are present in the poems of Hafez. There are two frequent terms used by him, first one is Peer-e Moghan (literally "the old man of the magi") and second one is Deyr-e Moghan (literally "the monastery of the magi").[9]

Greco-Roman sources
Hellenistic period
The oldest surviving Greek reference to the magi – from Greek μάγος (mágos, plural: magoi) – could be from 6th century BC Heraclitus (apud Clemens Protrepticus 2.22.2[10]), who cursed the magi for their "impious" rites and rituals.[11] A description of the rituals that Heraclitus refers to has not survived, and there is nothing to suggest that Heraclitus was referring to foreigners.

The Farnese Cup or Tazza Farnese is a 2nd-century BC cameo hardstone carving bowl or cup made in Hellenistic Egypt of four-layered sardonyx agate. It is at the Naples National Archaeological Museum.[1] It is about 20 cm (8 in) wide and similar in form to a Greek phiale or Roman patera, with no foot.[2][3] It features relief carvings on both its exterior and interior surfaces.[2][3]

There is no surviving evidence regarding when and why the piece was made, though there is consensus among scholars that it was created in Alexandria, due to the blending of Ancient Egyptian and Ancient Greek or Roman iconography found in its relief carvings. This provides a range of time wherein it may have been created, spanning from approximately 300 BC to 20 BC.[2][4]

The underside has a large Gorgon's head occupying most of the area, probably intended to ward off evil. The upper side has a scene with several figures that has long puzzled scholars. It seems clearly an allegory containing several divine figures and perhaps personifications, but corresponds to no other known representation and has been interpreted in several different ways.

History
The origin of the Tazza Farnese is unknown, leaving archaeologists and art historians to theorize a date and purpose for its creation. While its size and the material used are usually considered, theories of origin are mainly arrived at via individual analysis of the iconography of the piece, and therefore vary from one analysis to the next.[2][3][4]

Many archaeologists and art historians attribute the Tazza to the Hellenistic Period, asserting that its blending of Greek and Egyptian cultural symbols, as well as the funds necessary to commission such a large gemstone cameo, tie it to the Ptolemaic court.[4] Though not a widely held view, more recent analyses of the piece have assigned it a later date in the Augustan Period.[2][3]

After Octavian's conquest of Egypt in 31 BC, the Farnese Cup was possibly acquired by the Treasury of Rome; according to some, it was only made after the Romans took Egypt. It seems it was later taken to Byzantium, then back west after this city was sacked in 1204 during the Fourth Crusade. By 1239 it was in the court of Frederick II,[5] from which it then reached the Persian court of Herat or possibly Samarkand, where a contemporary drawing documents it;[6] thence it found its way to the court of Alfonso of Aragon in Naples, where Angelo Poliziano saw it in 1458. Lorenzo the Magnificent finally purchased the famous "scutella di calcedonio" in Rome, in 1471. From there it came into the possession of the Farnese family through Margaret of Austria and thus into the Naples National Archaeological Museum[1]

Lawsuit Filed Over Death of Wrestler at Kemper
The Kansas City Star - June 16, 1999
Christine Vendel
The Kansas City Star
6/16/1999

The harness that suspended Owen Hart was unsafe and inadequate to hold the 230-pound professional wrestler who fell to his death last month, a lawsuit filed Tuesday alleged.

Hart’s family named 13 defendants – including the World Wrestling Federation and the city of Kansas City – in the wrongful death lawsuit, filed in Jackson County Circuit Court. The lawsuit, which seeks an undetermined amount of money, stemmed from the May 23 accident that killed Hart at Kemper Arena.

Hart, 34, of Calgary, Alberta, was supposed to enter the ring from a catwalk 78 feet above the ring. As he dangled in mid-air, waiting for his cue, a quick-release mechanism on his vest opened prematurely, dropping him to his death, said police who investigated the accident.

The lawsuit alleged that the stunt was dangerous and poorly planned. In particular, the lawsuit alleged that the harness system was defective.

“Our legal and factual allegation is that Owen Hart died because this makeshift contraption was totally inadequate for this intended purpose,” family attorney Gary Robb said at a news conference. He said the mechanism used to support Hart was intended to rig sailboats.

Robb said Hart could have moved his shoulder and triggered the harness’ quick release mechanism on his vest. He said it took only six pounds of pressure to trigger the mechanism. In comparison, it takes eight pounds of pressure to pull the trigger of a Kansas City police officer’s handgun, according to police.

The 118-page lawsuit lists 46 separate counts against the defendants, who include the WWF; Vince McMahon, the WWF’s chairman; and the city, as owner of Kemper Arena.

The city is covered by an insurance policy paid for by the WWF. All arena Lessees are required to buy liability insurance to protect the city, said William LaMette, director of convention centers. City officials declined to comment further.

Other defendants in the lawsuit include WWF’s parent company, Titan Sports, four companies that manufactured or sold the harness – and – cable system and four riggers who set up the stunt. Three riggers were on the catwalk with Hart before he fell. The role of the FOURTH rigger was not clear.

Most of the defendants contacted Tuesday were not aware that they had been named in the lawsuit. Some declined to comment; others did not return telephone calls.

Besides the lawsuit, police are investigating whether criminal acts contributed to Hart’s death. Their investigation is focused on the appropriateness of the equipment used by Hart, to see whether any one was criminally negligent.

WWF spokesman Jim Byrne said his company had not yet been served with the lawsuit.

“It’s difficult to respond to a lawsuit that hasn’t been seen yet,” he said. “The police investigation is still ongoing, so it would seem the lawsuit is precipitous.”

Byrne declined to discuss the equipment used by Hart. He said Hart had performed the stunt a few times before.

The lawsuit claimed precautions were missing, such as a safety net, safety harness, backup cables or a safety lock on the release mechanism. Owen Hart also was not properly trained, the lawsuit said. “What happened to Owen Hart was absolutely preventable,” said Pamela Fischer, a family attorney from Canada.

The lawsuit was filed on behalf of Hart’s widow, Martha Hart; their two children, ages 7 and 3; and Owen Hart’s parents, all of Calgary.

🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Week 22 (Days 148 to 154): Phase Three: A Face Takes Shape
🌱 This week: your baby's face looks more and more like a newborn's, with eyebrows, eyelashes, and clearer lips, while the eyelids stay closed. The hands can grip, and the inner ear helps your baby sense balance. Your baby is about 11 inches from head to heel and weighs about 15 ounces, about the size of a papaya.
⚕️ Source: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. To maintain medical accuracy, every lesson is fact-checked by Grok (Sal). General pregnancy education only, not medical advice. Always talk with your doctor or midwife.

💡 If you could see your baby's face this week, you would see eyebrows, tiny eyelashes, and lips. The eyes are still sealed shut. But the face you will kiss for the rest of your life is already there. What is the first word you will sing over it?

👶 Where your baby is this week

If conception happened around day 14, your baby is 134 to 140 days old this week. Last week your baby practiced tasting and moving. This week the face comes into focus.

Fine eyebrows and eyelashes are growing. The lips are more defined, and tooth buds are forming under the gums. The eyelids are still fused shut, and they usually open around Week 26 to 28.

The tiny hands can now grip, and your baby may hold the umbilical cord. The inner ear is developed enough to help your baby sense up and down. Your baby is about 11 inches from head to heel and weighs about 15 ounces.

🤰 Your body this week

Your belly button may start to flatten or pop out. Stretch marks, heartburn, and swollen feet at the end of the day are common. Keep your feet up when you can.

Many doctors check blood sugar between Weeks 24 and 28, so ask at your next visit when your glucose test is. Call your doctor or midwife right away for bleeding, leaking fluid, regular tightenings, a severe headache, or changes in your vision.

🎵 Why singing, not talking

Talking needs understanding. Singing is melody, rhythm, and pitch, and those can be received before understanding arrives. Hearing usually begins between about Week 18 and Week 26, and word meaning comes after birth. From conception your baby is a spirit being, and GUP songs go spirit to spirit.

GUP songs are baby music with a purpose: gentle like lullabies, repeating like nursery rhymes, and full of phonic songs the whole family can sing. This is your child's first kids music.

🔤 Phase Three: face words

This week, sing face words. "Eye." "Nose." "Lip." "Chin." Touch your own face as you sing each one. After birth you will sing the same words while you touch your baby's face, and the song will already be home.

📖 One song, three ways

Morning: hear the Week-22 song and thank God for your baby's face. Midday: hum it with headphones on, then sing one face word to the tune. Evening: write your face words on your Word List page with the phonograms they came from.

Dad, headphones on you too. Sing "nose" and "chin" with her.

🙏 Pray and remember

📜 “May the Lord reveal his face to you and take pity on you.” (Numbers 6:25, CPDV)

⭐ “Audrey Hepburn was born May 4, 1929. She went hungry as a child during World War II, became one of the most famous faces in film, and spent her later years serving the world's children for UNICEF.”

🙏 "Father God, thank You for the face You are shaping. Let it one day shine with Your joy. Let our voices be the first music it knows. In Jesus' name, amen."

🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Deep Dive: Week 22 (Days 148 to 154): Phase Three: A Face Takes Shape

🔎 Week 22 at a Glance

Week 22 is pregnancy days 148 to 154, counted from the first day of your last period, the same count your doctor, midwife, and pregnancy calculator use. If conception happened around day 14, your baby is between 134 and 140 days old. In longer or shorter cycles, these days shift a little.

This is the week of the face. Eyebrows and eyelashes are growing, the lips are clearer, and tooth buds sit under the gums. The eyes are formed, but the eyelids are still sealed. The hands can grip. The inner ear is developed enough to help with balance. The skin is still thin and wrinkled, with little fat under it yet.

Your baby is about 11 inches from head to heel and weighs about 15 ounces, almost a pound, about the size of a papaya. Your baby now looks much like a tiny newborn, only thinner.

⏳ The Week, Day by Day

Here is the week counted in days after conception. In a 28-day cycle, add 14 to find your pregnancy day. Babies grow at their own pace, so treat this as a guide.

Days 134 and 135 (pregnancy days 148 and 149): Eyebrows and eyelashes keep growing. They are fine and pale at first.

Days 136 and 137 (days 150 and 151): The lips are more defined. Under the gums, tooth buds for the baby teeth are forming, and the buds for adult teeth begin to form behind them.

Day 138 (day 152): The hands are more active. Your baby may grip the umbilical cord or touch the face.

Day 139 (day 153): The inner ear helps your baby sense position, so your baby can tell which way is up as you move.

Day 140 (day 154): Your baby weighs about 15 ounces and is about 11 inches from head to heel.

😊 The Face God Is Making

Picture a face without eyebrows, without eyelashes, without the curve of the lips. Now picture those features slowly appearing. That is what is happening this week. The face your baby will wear for life is being finished, line by line.

Eyebrows and eyelashes grow in fine and light at first. They will darken later. The lips are fuller and better formed, and the little mouth often opens and closes. On a detailed ultrasound, some parents catch what looks like a frown, a squint, or a pout. These are early muscle movements as the nerves of the face connect with the brain.

The nose, the chin, and the shape of the ears are all clearer now. Many parents start to see family features in the ultrasound pictures. Whose nose is it? Whose chin? That conversation may go on for years.

God told Moses to have the priests bless the people by asking the Lord to shine His face on them. Before your child ever sees your face, God has already turned His face toward your child.

👁️ Eyes Formed, Lids Still Closed

Your baby's eyes are formed, and the parts inside them keep developing. But the eyelids are still fused shut. They protect the delicate eyes while they finish growing. The lids usually open around Week 26 to 28.

Even with the lids closed, the eyes move. Over the coming weeks, these eye movements will become part of your baby's sleep patterns.

The iris, the colored part of the eye, does not have much color yet. Many babies are born with blue or gray eyes that change color over the first year, as pigment builds up. So do not be surprised if the eye color you see at birth is not the color your child keeps.

🦷 Tooth Buds Under the Gums

Under your baby's gums, the buds for all twenty baby teeth have already formed, and the buds for many adult teeth are starting behind them. Teeth usually do not come through until around six months after birth, but the plan for them is already in place.

Your baby takes calcium and other minerals from your blood to build these teeth and bones. Keep eating calcium-rich foods such as milk, yogurt, pasteurized cheese, fortified plant milks, tofu made with calcium, and leafy greens. Most pregnant women need about 1,000 milligrams of calcium a day.

Your own teeth matter too. Brush twice a day, floss daily, and keep your dental checkups. Dental cleanings are safe in pregnancy. Tell your dentist you are pregnant.

✋ Hands That Grip

Your baby's hands have grown from tiny paddles into fingers with nails. Now the hands are getting stronger, and your baby may grip the umbilical cord, touch the face, or bring a hand to the mouth.

This grip is the start of the grasp reflex. After birth, if you place your finger in your newborn's palm, those little fingers will curl around it and hold on. Many parents say that first grip is the moment their heart melted.

The prophet Isaiah wrote that God has engraved His people on the palms of His hands. Before your baby ever grips your finger, your child is already held in the hands of God.

📜 “Behold, I have engraved you on my hands. Your walls are always before my eyes.” (Isaiah 49:16, CPDV)

⭐ “Simone Biles was born March 14, 1997. With hands that grip the bars and an inner sense of balance that seems to know where she is in the air, she became the most decorated gymnast in history.”

⚖️ The Inner Ear and Balance

The inner ear does two jobs. One part helps with hearing. Another part, made of tiny fluid-filled loops, senses motion and position. It tells the brain which way is up and when the head is turning.

By now, this balance system is developed enough to work. When you walk, turn, bend, or lie down, your baby can sense the change. The gentle rocking of your daily movement is your baby's first ride.

This may be one reason many newborns calm down when they are rocked, swayed, or carried. That motion feels like the womb. Rocking your baby while you sing lullabies and soft baby music after birth will feel like coming home.

🧬 Skin, Fat, and Growth

Your baby's skin is still thin, wrinkled, and somewhat see-through, with a pinkish-red color from the blood vessels underneath. That is because there is very little fat under the skin yet.

That will change. From now on, your baby will put on weight quickly. Fat begins to build up under the skin, smoothing out the wrinkles and helping your baby keep warm after birth. Between now and birth, your baby's weight will grow about seven times over.

You do not need to eat for two adults to make this happen. You need good food, steady meals, and the extra amount your doctor recommends, usually about 340 more calories a day in this trimester.

🧠 A Brain That Folds

Your baby's brain has been growing fast for months. Until now its surface has been mostly smooth. In the second half of pregnancy, the surface begins to fold into the ridges and grooves you see in pictures of an adult brain.

Those folds let a large amount of brain fit inside a small skull. The main grooves begin to appear around this stage, and more form over the coming weeks, all the way to birth. Each fold adds room for the brain cells that will one day help your child see, move, think, speak, and read.

This is quiet work. You cannot feel it the way you feel a kick. But it is some of the most important building happening inside you right now. Keep taking your prenatal vitamin, eat good fats from low-mercury fish a couple of times a week, and rest. You are feeding a growing mind.

🤲 Touch Through the Belly

Many mothers rub or pat their belly without thinking about it. It turns out your baby may notice. In one study, researchers watched babies on ultrasound between about Week 21 and Week 33. When the mothers stroked their bellies, the babies moved their arms, heads, and mouths more than when no one touched the belly.

Your touch, your voice, and your movement all reach your baby. Touch is one of the earliest senses to develop, and it is one of the ways God built for you to connect with your child before you meet.

Try this during the weekly song: put on your headphones, rest your hand on your belly, and slowly stroke in time with the music. Dad can do the same. When your baby kicks back, write it in your journal.

🔤 Phase Three: Face Words

In Week 20 you joined sounds into "mama" and "dada." In Week 21 you made food words. This week, Phase Three moves to the face. Face words are some of the earliest words children learn, because parents point to them and name them every day.

Start with short ones. "Eye" is one long sound. "Nose" is "n," "o," and "s." "Lip" is "l," "i," and "p." "Chin" is "ch," "i," and "n." Find each phonogram on your First Sounds list, then sing the word on the melody of the weekly song.

As you sing, touch your own face. Eye, nose, lip, chin. After birth, you will sing the same words as you gently touch your baby's face. The tune, the words, and the touch will come together. These are the simplest phonic songs there are, the kind of nursery rhymes and kids music every family makes up.

Write each face word on your Word List page with the phonograms it came from.

📜 “Write the vision and explain it on tablets.” (Habakkuk 2:2, CPDV)

⭐ “George Washington was born February 22, 1732. As a teenager he copied out by hand more than one hundred rules of good manners and respect, and he grew up to become the first president of the United States.”

🤰 Your Body at Twenty-Two Weeks

Your womb is now about an inch or so above your belly button. As your belly grows, the belly button may flatten or pop out. It usually goes back after birth.

Many mothers feel more swelling in the feet and ankles by the end of the day. This is common because your body is holding more fluid. Put your feet up, avoid standing still for a long time, wear comfortable shoes, and lie on your side to rest. Call your doctor right away if swelling comes on suddenly, especially in your face or hands, or if one leg is much more swollen than the other.

Other changes may include heartburn, constipation, backaches, and itchy skin on the belly as it stretches. A gentle, fragrance-free lotion can help itchy skin. Call your doctor if you have severe itching, especially on the palms of your hands or soles of your feet, because that can be a sign of a liver condition in pregnancy.

🩸 Blood Type and Your Visits

Early in pregnancy, your blood was tested for your blood type. If your blood is Rh-negative, your doctor will usually give you a shot called Rh immune globulin around Week 28, and again after birth if your baby is Rh-positive. This protects future pregnancies.

Your doctor may also check your iron again later in pregnancy. Keep eating iron-rich foods with a vitamin C food at the same meal.

Your glucose screening test is usually between Weeks 24 and 28. Ask at your next visit when yours will be and whether you need to do anything special to prepare.

🌗 Skin Changes in Pregnancy

Pregnancy hormones can change your skin. Many mothers notice darker skin on the nipples, a dark line down the belly called the linea nigra, and patches of darker skin on the face, sometimes called the mask of pregnancy. These usually fade after birth.

Sunlight can make the dark patches on the face darker. Wear a wide-brimmed hat and use sunscreen when you are outside. Ask your doctor before using any skin creams with strong ingredients, since some acne and anti-aging products are not safe in pregnancy.

Stretch marks are common too, and many depend on your family's skin. Lotions may help itchy skin feel better, though they may not prevent stretch marks. Over time after birth, stretch marks usually fade to lighter lines. They are marks of the life you carried.

🧠 Foggy Days

Many mothers say they feel forgetful or foggy during pregnancy. You walk into a room and forget why. You misplace your keys. This is common, and tiredness and poor sleep often play a part.

Keep a simple list on your phone or in your journal. Put your keys, glasses, and phone in the same place every day. Set reminders for appointments and your prenatal vitamin. Rest when you can.

Be gentle with yourself. Your body and mind are doing a great deal of work. God is not grading you on how well you remember where you put your shoes.

🛁 Warm Baths, Not Hot Tubs

A warm bath can ease sore muscles and help you relax. Keep the water warm, not hot, and get out if you feel dizzy or overheated.

Hot tubs and saunas are a different matter. They can raise your body temperature too much, which may harm a growing baby, especially early in pregnancy. Most doctors advise avoiding them throughout pregnancy. If you are unsure, ask your doctor.

👟 Growing Feet

Many mothers find their shoes feel tight by the middle of pregnancy. Swelling is part of it, but pregnancy hormones also loosen the ligaments in the feet, and the extra weight can flatten the arches. For some women, the feet stay a half size larger after birth.

Wear comfortable, supportive shoes with low, wide heels and room for your toes. Avoid standing in one place for long periods. Put your feet up when you rest, and do gentle ankle circles to keep the blood moving. Comfortable feet make it easier to keep walking, and walking is good for you and your baby.

🎨 A Picture of Your Baby's Face

On a page in your journal, sketch or describe the face you imagine your baby will have. Whose eyes? Whose smile? It does not need to be good art. After birth, come back and compare. It is a sweet way to remember this week, when the face was first coming into shape.

🥗 Body: Caring for the Home This Week

This week, give your plate a calcium and protein focus for your baby's teeth, bones, and growing muscles. Yogurt, milk, pasteurized cheese, beans, eggs cooked firm, chicken, and fish all help. Add plenty of fiber from vegetables, fruit, and whole grains to keep constipation away, and keep a water bottle with you through the day.

Keep food safety simple: wash produce, cook meats and eggs all the way, and heat deli meats and hot dogs until steaming. Pick pasteurized dairy. Enjoy low-mercury fish such as salmon, sardines, or trout two or three times a week, and skip shark, swordfish, king mackerel, and tilefish.

No amount of alcohol is known to be safe while you are pregnant. Stay away from smoking, vaping, and secondhand smoke. Keep caffeine under 200 mg a day. Check with your doctor before taking any medicine, herb, or supplement, and keep up gentle movement if your doctor says it is safe.

🚨 Signs to Call About Now

Call your doctor or midwife right away if you have regular tightenings or cramps, pressure low in the pelvis, a new low backache that comes and goes, bleeding, or fluid leaking from the vagina. These can be signs of labor starting too early.

Also call right away for a severe headache, changes in your vision, sudden swelling of the face or hands, pain high in the belly on the right side, a fever, pain or burning when you pass urine, or a big drop in your baby's movement once you have felt regular movement.

You know your body. If something feels wrong, call. That is not overreacting. That is taking care of your child.

👨 For Dad: Learn Her Face

Dad, your baby's face is taking shape, and soon you will see it. For now, look at hers. Pregnancy brings tired days, swollen feet, and nights of broken sleep. Learn to read her face. Notice when she is worn out, and step in before she has to ask.

Rub her feet at night. Bring her water. Take over the dishes. Then sit beside her, put on your headphones, and sing face words with her: "eye," "nose," "chin." Touch her face as you sing, and let her touch yours. One day your child will learn these words from both of you.

Your voice is deep, and deep sounds travel well through the body. As hearing grows over the coming weeks, your voice is becoming part of the sound of home.

👵 For Grandparents and Siblings

Big brothers and sisters can be face word teachers. Let them point to their own eyes, nose, and chin and sing the words with Mom, like their own kids music. Ask them whose nose they think the baby will have.

Grandparents can bring out family baby pictures. Look at the faces together. Write in the journal which family faces you hope to see in this new one.

🎶 One Song, Three Ways: Week 22

Every week has one GUP song, learned three different ways. A good preschool teacher never teaches an important lesson only once. Teach it three ways, and it is remembered.

Hear it. In the morning, listen once with your eyes closed. Thank God for the face He is finishing.

Hum it. At midday, put on headphones and hum along. Then sing "eye, nose, lip, chin" to the tune, touching each one as you sing.

Write it. In the evening, listen with your Pregnancy Journal open. Write the phonograms you hear, and build one face word from them for your Word List page.

GUP songs are baby music with a purpose: gentle like lullabies, repeating like nursery rhymes, and full of the phonic songs that become the building blocks of reading.

📓 Your Pregnancy Journal: Week-22 Pages

On your Word List page, add this week's face words with the phonograms they came from.

On a "Family Faces" page, write which family features you think your baby will have, and whose eyes, nose, or chin. After birth, come back and write what you see.

On your "Movement" page, write when your baby moves most this week. Add your questions about the glucose test and your next visit. Write a prayer for your baby's face.

🧭 God's GPS

Every pregnancy has its own road. Some mothers sail through the second trimester. Others fight swelling, heartburn, or worry the whole way. You may have planned one kind of pregnancy and be living another.

That is all right. You make the plans, and God directs the steps. He sees the road ahead even when you cannot.

📜 “The heart of man disposes his way. But it is for the Lord to direct his steps.” (Proverbs 16:9, CPDV)

⭐ “Whitney Houston was born August 9, 1963. She first sang in the choir of New Hope Baptist Church in Newark, New Jersey, where her mother led the music, and became one of the best-selling singers of all time.”

💭 When Worry Comes

As your baby grows, it is normal to worry. Will the baby be healthy? Will I be a good mother? Can we afford this? Will birth go well? Many mothers carry these questions quietly.

Write your worries in your journal. Then write a prayer underneath each one. Talk with your husband, a friend, or someone at church. Bring health questions to your doctor rather than searching for the worst case online.

If you feel sad, hopeless, anxious, or unable to enjoy things most days for more than two weeks, tell your doctor or midwife. Depression and anxiety in pregnancy are common and treatable. Asking for help is not a lack of faith. It is wisdom, and it is care for your child.

🛋️ Rest Is Not Laziness

In the second half of pregnancy, your body is doing more work every day, even when you are sitting still. Resting is not wasting time. It is part of the job.

Take short rests through the day. Lie on your side when you can. Put your feet up after work. Say yes when someone offers to help. Jesus invited the tired to come to Him for rest, and that invitation includes tired mothers.

📜 “Come to me, all you who labor and have been burdened, and I will refresh you.” (Matthew 11:28, CPDV)

⭐ “Shirley Temple was born April 23, 1928. Her dimpled smile made her the most famous child star of her time, and as a grown woman she served her country as a United States ambassador.”

🙏 A Prayer for Week 22

🙏 "Father God, thank You for the face You are finishing in secret: the eyebrows, the lashes, the lips, the little chin. Thank You for hands that grip and for the inner ear that knows which way is up.

Turn Your face toward our child and be gracious. Keep our baby growing strong. Give rest to the body that carries this child. Let the words we sing become words our child one day says, and let that face light up with joy at the sound of Your name. In Jesus' name, amen."

❓ Questions Parents Ask

Can my baby see yet? The eyes are formed, but the eyelids stay closed until about Week 26 to 28. Even then, there is not much to see in the womb except changes in light.

Why does my baby look so thin on the ultrasound? There is very little fat under the skin yet. From now on, fat builds up quickly, and your baby will fill out over the coming weeks.

Is it normal for my feet to swell? Mild swelling in the feet and ankles at the end of the day is common. Call your doctor right away if swelling is sudden, if it is in your face or hands, or if one leg is much more swollen than the other.

Do I need to do anything for my baby's teeth now? Eat calcium-rich foods and take your prenatal vitamin. Take care of your own teeth and gums too.

When do I call my doctor right away? Call for bleeding, leaking fluid, regular tightenings, pelvic pressure, a severe headache, vision changes, sudden swelling of the face or hands, severe itching, a fever, or much less movement than usual.

✅ Your Week-22 Checklist

I took my prenatal vitamin every day. I ate calcium-rich foods and plenty of fiber. I put my feet up. I asked when my glucose test will be.

I heard, hummed, and wrote this week's one song every day. I sang face words and touched my face as I sang. I added face words to my Word List. Dad sang with me. The family guessed whose nose the baby will have.

⚕️ Source: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. To maintain medical accuracy, every lesson is fact-checked by Grok (Sal). General pregnancy education only, not medical advice. Always talk with your doctor or midwife.

text:
Somewhere in corporate America, a hiring manager welcomed a new employee on Monday morning and discovered the person they hired had apparently been swapped out like a defective toaster. 

At this point, I’m surprised HR doesn’t inspect new hires for a serial number and an original receipt. Someone recently shared a hiring story with me that made my coffee file for workers’ compensation. Apparently, a fake applicant used an avatar to make it through FOUR video interviews, reached the CFO, received an offer, and then an entirely different human showed up for the first day of work. Four interviews. A CFO. An offer. And the grand finale was a surprise guest appearance from someone who wasn’t even in the original cast.

Meanwhile, actual candidates with actual faces, actual experience, and actual electric bills can’t get a recruiter to answer an email. I’ve applied to positions where my resume apparently offended the applicant tracking system before a human could see it. But an avatar allegedly sailed through four rounds like it had a platinum membership to the hiring circus. I would love to know its secret. Did it say it was passionate about synergy? Did it list “being a team player” under special abilities? Was its greatest weakness caring too much, or having a different person inside the computer?

And the interview panel! Nobody noticed anything unusual? Not one executive leaned toward the screen and said, “Interesting. Your facial expressions seem to be buffering.” Maybe they were too busy asking where the candidate sees themselves in five years. The correct answer, apparently, is “somewhere else, because I’m not technically here right now.” Imagine the CFO approving the hire after asking fourteen questions about cultural alignment, only to discover the company had recruited a plot twist.

I’m also hearing about applications arriving with resumes that literally say TEST, and work histories listing ACME. ACME! That’s not a career history. That’s where Wile E. Coyote orders rockets. If a cartoon supply company is now qualifying people for interviews, my inner raccoon would like to submit his application. He has experience in waste management, conflict resolution, and entering buildings without authorization. Leadership potential, obviously.

To be clear, fake applicants and identity tricks are a serious problem. Employers should absolutely protect themselves. But there is something spectacularly ironic about a hiring process that demands five references, three assessments, eight passwords, and proof you’ve been breathing since 1997, yet can still struggle to establish who is actually sitting in the interview. We’ve built a system that can reject a qualified person in six seconds and apparently needs four meetings to recognize a screensaver wearing a blazer.

To every real candidate still waiting on a callback, I see you. Keep your sense of humor. And if your next interview includes an avatar, ask whether the job comes with stunt double benefits.

Total lies. Time to debunk this once and for all. Thread 🧵

>>>> Part 1 <<<<

I. INTRODUCTION: THE CONFESSIONAL MYTH VERSUS THE SOVEREIGN LEDGER

The collapse of the Byzantine Empire on 29 May 1453 was not the result of an eleventh hour religious betrayal at a city gate,

it was the terminal bankruptcy liquidation of a state that had surrendered its customs revenues, monetary sovereignty, and credit supply to foreign merchant banking syndicates over the preceding 371 years.

In popular polemics, a persistent claim asserts that the Byzantine Empire endured for a millennium because it excluded Jews from state administration, and that it fell only because its Jewish inhabitants opened the gates of Constantinople to the Ottoman armies of Sultan Mehmed II.

But when subjected to actual historical methodology, that is, testing rhetorical claims against surviving state treaties, treasury ledgers, notarial cartularies, and eyewitness siege diaries, this claim collapses completely.

1. The Forensic Origin of the "Opened Gates" Myth

No contemporary eyewitness to the siege of 1453, whether Greek, Venetian, Genoese, or Ottoman, records any Jewish involvement in breaching or opening the defenses of Constantinople. We possess the daily diary of the Venetian surgeon Niccolò Barbaro (Giornale dell'assedio di Costantinopoli), the memoirs of the close imperial adviser George Sphrantzes (Chronicon Minus), the report of the Catholic Archbishop Leonard of Chios to Pope Nicholas V, the history of Doukas (Historia Turco-Byzantina), and the Ottoman accounts of Tursun Beg and Aşıkpaşazade.

Every single one of these primary witnesses confirms the same material facts:

•The outer land walls were pulverized in the Mesoteichion sector by massive bronze siege cannons cast by Orban, a Christian Hungarian engineer. Orban had originally offered his services to the Byzantine Emperor Constantine XI Palaiologos, but defected to the Ottomans because the bankrupt Byzantine treasury could not pay his minuscule stipend or afford the raw bronze required for his foundry.

•The only gate left unbolted on the morning of 29 May 1453 was a small postern in the Blachernae wall known as the Kerkoporta. As documented by Doukas (Chapter 39), this gate had been reopened by Christian Byzantine and Genoese defenders (commanded by the Italian Bocchiardi brothers) so they could launch a tactical sortie against the Ottoman flank; in the chaos of their retreat, the Christian soldiers failed to bolt it behind them.

•Meanwhile, the Romaniote and Karaite Jewish communities of Constantinople, residing in quarters such as Vlanga and Chalkoprateia, held neither military command over the walls nor political office. When the city fell, they were subjected to looting, captivity, and forced imperial resettlement (sürgün) alongside the Christian Greek population, as recorded in Sultan Mehmed II’s 1455 cadastral survey (Tapu Tahrir Defteri TT 1M).

Where, then, did the myth of "Jews opening the gates" originate ?

It is a documented literary fabrication transplanted from medieval Spain. In the 13th century, 500 years after the Umayyad conquest of Visigothic Hispania in 711 CE, the Christian chronicler Lucas de Tuy (Chronicon Mundi, c. 1236) invented the story that the Jews of Toledo had opened the city gates to Muslim forces while the Christians were at church on Palm Sunday. Modern polemicists simply lifted this medieval Iberian trope and pasted it onto 1453 Constantinople.

2. Why the Myth Exists: Hiding the Balance-Sheet Crime

Why would a fabricated confessional story be used to explain the fall of an empire 

Because blaming a religious minority for a sudden act of treason conceals a slow, structural, and thoroughly documented financial crime.

A state does not survive on titles, crowns, or religious orthodoxy. It survives on fiscal and logistical capacity, its ability to collect taxes in hard currency, maintain a stable coinage, fund a standing military, and control its own credit markets. 

Whenever a sovereign retains the legal mandate to rule while surrendering the financial capacity to private merchant banking syndicates, the sovereign ceases to be the master of the state and becomes a debtor accepting terms.

——> Between 1082 and 1453, the Byzantine Empire was systematically hollowed out, NOT by its Jewish subjects, and not initially by its Muslim neighbours, but by Christian Italian merchant banking republics, principally Venice and Genoa.

————————

II. THE FISCAL BASELINE: HOW THE BYZANTINE STATE ACTUALLY FUNDED ITSELF (312–1071)

To understand how the Byzantine Empire was bankrupted, a reader unfamiliar with medieval economic history must first understand why the empire was once the richest superpower in the Western world. For over seven centuries, Byzantine state power rested on a closed, state-controlled fiscal circuit with three pillars:

1) The Kommerkion (The 10% Customs and Transaction Tax):

Constantinople sat at the geographic choke point between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean, and between Europe and Asia. Every merchant ship passing through the Bosporus and every wholesale commodity traded in the markets of the empire was subject to the kommerkion, an imperial customs and sales duty fixed at 10% ad valorem (10% of the value of the goods), payable in hard gold coin. This provided the Imperial Treasury (Sakellion) with a massive, continuous stream of liquid cash.

2) The Land Tax (Kapnikon and Synone) Paid in Gold:

Free peasant smallholders across Anatolia (modern Turkey) and the Balkans paid their land and hearth taxes directly to imperial tax collectors in gold coin. The state then paid its provincial soldiers (stratiotai) and bureaucracy in that same gold coin, which the soldiers spent in local markets, allowing the peasants to earn back the gold needed to pay the next year's taxes.

3) The Nomisma / Solidus (720 Years of Undebased Gold):

From the reign of Constantine the Great (312 CE) until the 1030s, the Byzantine gold coin—the nomisma (or solidus)—was the "US Dollar" of the medieval world.

Struck at 72 coins to the Roman pound of pure gold at a purity of 23.5 to 24 carats, it never fluctuated. 

Foreign merchants were legally forbidden from exporting gold bullion out of the empire, and strict state guilds (documented in the 10th-century Book of the Eparch [Eparchikon Biblion]) regulated silk, banking, bullion exchange, and food prices to prevent private cartels from cornering the market.

The Structural Vulnerability: As long as the Emperor controlled the 10% kommerkion, maintained a native navy, and kept the domestic guilds under state law, no foreign syndicate could capture the empire. The demolition began the moment the state outsourced its military logistics in exchange for tax exemptions.

———————

III. THE 1082 TRAP: THE IMPERIAL CHRYSOBULL AND THE ALIENATION OF THE TAX BASE

1. The Historical Crisis (1071–1082)

In the 1070s, the Byzantine Empire suffered a dual military shock: Seljuk Turks overran the tax producing interior of Anatolia after the Battle of Manzikert (1071), while Norman armies from southern Italy (led by Robert Guiscard) invaded the western Balkans across the Adriatic Sea (1081).

When Emperor Alexios I Komnenos seized the throne in 1081, the Imperial Treasury was exhausted, and the neglected Byzantine navy could not stop the Norman fleet from supplying its invading army. 

Desperate for immediate naval capacity, Alexios I turned to the Republic of Venice, a rising maritime merchant oligarchy whose merchant galley fleets could double as warships.

2. The Primary Document: The Golden Bull (Chrysobullon Sigillion) of May 1082

Venice agreed to provide naval support, but it did not ask for a simple cash fee. Instead, Venetian negotiators demanded a permanent structural concession inside the Byzantine tax code.

In May 1082, Alexios I signed an imperial decree sealed in gold—the Chrysobull of 1082 (preserved in its Latin translation inside the Venetian State Archives: Archivio di Stato di Venezia [ASV], Secreta, Pacta, Liber Albus, fols. 1–3, published in https://t.co/D9QZ5bwzue. Tafel and G.M. Thomas, Urkunden zur älteren Handels- und Staatsgeschichte der Republik Venedig, Vienna, 1856, Vol. I, Doc. XXIII, pp. 51–54).

The clauses of the 1082 Chrysobull executed a fiscal revolution:

•Total Exemption from the 10% Kommerkion: Venetian merchants were granted complete, perpetual exemption from the 10% customs and transaction tax (kommerkion) as well as all harbour, transit, and docking fees (xylokalamon, limeniatikon, poriatikon) across 30 major ports and cities of the Byzantine Empire, including Constantinople itself.

•Sovereign Real Estate Inside the Capital: The Emperor ceded an entire commercial district (embolon) along the Golden Horn inside Constantinople—complete with warehouses, three maritime landing stages (skalai), bakeries, and churches—directly to Venetian jurisdiction.

•Direct Treasury Subsidies to Foreign Elites: The Byzantine treasury bound itself to pay annual gold stipends out of state revenues to the Doge of Venice (who was given the imperial title Protosebastos) and the Patriarch of Grado.

3. The Mechanical Consequence: Tax Free Arbitrage Destroys Domestic Revenue

Examine the arithmetic of what the 1082 Chrysobull did to the Byzantine economy:

•A native Greek or Jewish merchant in Constantinople importing or exporting 1,000 gold hyperpyra worth of silk, grain, or spices had to pay 100 hyperpyra (10%) to the Imperial Treasury at the customs house, plus harbour fees.

•A Venetian merchant operating from his tax free wharf on the Golden Horn paid 0 hyperpyra (0%) on the exact same cargo.

Because Venetian merchants enjoyed a statutory 10% price advantage over every domestic Byzantine subject, Greek merchants were systematically driven out of wholesale maritime trade or forced to act as subordinate middlemen for Venetian houses. Worse still, as trade volume shifted from tax paying Byzantine merchants to tax exempt Venetian syndicates, every ship that docked at the Venetian quarter represented a 100% loss of customs revenue to the Byzantine state.

By outsourcing its naval capacity in 1082, the Byzantine Crown had built a legal trap: it had given a foreign merchant syndicate a permanent tax exemption that starved the very treasury needed to rebuild a native Byzantine navy.

————————

IV. THE REBELLION AGAINST THE CARTEL AND THE PATH TO 1204 (1118–1203)

Over the next century, successive Byzantine emperors realized that the 1082 Chrysobull was a fiscal death sentence and repeatedly tried to break the Venetian stranglehold—only to discover that once a state surrenders its logistical capacity, its creditors will use force to prevent the restoration of sovereignty:

1. The First Attempted Refusal (1118–1126):

Upon taking the throne in 1118, Emperor John II Komnenos refused to renew the 1082 Chrysobull, attempting to reimpose the 10% kommerkion on Venice. Venice responded immediately by deploying its battle fleet to raid and plunder the Byzantine islands of Rhodes, Chios, Samos, Lesbos, and Cephalonia. Lacking a fleet to stop the economic devastation, John II capitulated in August 1126 (ASV, Pacta, Liber Albus; Tafel & Thomas, Vol. I, No. XLIII), re-signing the 1082 tax exemptions in full.

2. The "Divide and Rule" Trap (1111 & 1155):

To dilute Venice’s monopoly, the Komnenian emperors granted partial customs reductions (reducing the 10% kommerkion to 4%) to Venice’s Italian rivals: Pisa (1111) and Genoa (1155).

Instead of saving the treasury, this multiplied the revenue haemorrhage. Now three competing Italian merchant republics held extraterritorial quarters along the Golden Horn, turning Constantinople’s waterfront into a battleground of rival foreign syndicates.

3. The 1171 Seizure and Sovereign Debt Settlement (1171–1189):

On 12 March 1171, Emperor Manuel I Komnenos launched a desperate state crack down: in a single day, imperial troops arrested thousands of Venetians across the empire and confiscated their ships, real estate, and merchandise to reclaim state control.

◦The Venetian response was not merely naval; it was financial. To fund a retaliatory fleet, Venice instituted the Camera degli Imprestiti (1171–1172), the earliest institutionalized system of compulsory, interest bearing transferable state bonds in Europe (documented in Gino Luzzatto, Il debito pubblico della Repubblica di Venezia).

◦Facing pressure on all fronts, subsequent emperors (Andronikos I and Isaac II Angelos) were forced not only to restore all Venetian tax exemptions (Chrysobulls of February 1187 and June 1189, ASV, Pacta; Tafel & Thomas, Vol. I, Nos. LXX–LXXIV), but to acknowledge a massive sovereign indemnity debt of 1,500 pounds of gold (108,000 gold hyperpyra) payable to Venice in instalments as compensation for the 1171 confiscations.

4. The 1198 Total Capitulation:

By November 1198, when Emperor Alexios III Angelos issued his Chrysobull to Doge Enrico Dandolo (ASV, Pacta; Tafel & Thomas, Vol. I, No. LXXXV), 200 pounds of gold on the 1171 indemnity remained unpaid. The 1198 treaty expanded Venice’s tax free zones across the entire interior of the Byzantine Empire and granted Venetian courts extraterritorial jurisdiction over disputes involving Byzantine subjects.

——————

V. THE 1204 ARMED FORECLOSURE: THE FOURTH CRUSADE AS A DEBT COLLECTION OPERATION

Mainstream textbooks often portray the Fourth Crusade (1202–1204), in which Western Christian crusaders sacked Christian Constantinople instead of fighting in Egypt or Jerusalem, as a tragic "diversion" or a "misunderstanding."

——> But when read through the primary contracts preserved in the Venetian archives and the eyewitness memoirs of Geoffrey of Villehardouin (De la Conquête de Constantinople) and Robert of Clari, the event reveals itself as the most ruthless sovereign debt foreclosure in medieval history.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

[April 1201: Treaty of Venice]

Crusaders contract for 33,500 troops → Owe Venice 85,000 Cologne Silver Marks

👇🏻

(August 1202: Crusaders short by 34,000 Silver Marks at Venice)

[Default #1: The Zara Diversion]

Doge Enrico Dandolo suspends debt in exchange for sacking rival Christian port of Zara
 
👇🏻

(Spring 1203: Treaty of Zara with exiled Byzantine Prince Alexios IV)

[The Sovereign Bailout Promise]

Alexios IV promises 200,000 Silver Marks + payment of Crusader debt to Venice

👇🏻

(July 1203 – Jan 1204: Alexios IV installed, finds Byzantine Treasury empty)

[Default #2: Sovereign Insolvency]

After melting church plate & icons, 100,000 Silver Marks remain unpaid

👇🏻

(March–April 1204: The Pact of March 1204 & Partition Treaty)

[Armed Receivership & Liquidation]

Creditors storm Constantinople (12–13 April 1204), seize ⅜ of the Empire & all customs houses

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Simplifying :

1. The Primary Contract: The Treaty of Venice (April 1201)

In April 1201 (ASV, Pacta I; Tafel & Thomas, Vol. I, No. XCII), six French envoys signed a binding commercial transport and provisioning contract with Doge Enrico Dandolo and the Republic of Venice:

•Venice agreed to suspend all its commercial trade for over a year to build, equip, and provision a massive fleet capable of transporting 4,500 knights, 4,500 horses, 9,000 squires, and 20,000 foot soldiers (33,500 men in total).

•In exchange, the Crusaders signed a fixed nominal debt obligation to pay Venice 85,000 Cologne marks of pure silver (roughly 20 metric tons of fine silver, more than twice the entire annual royal revenue of the King of England or France at the time) by April 1202.

2. The First Default and the Refinancing Trap (Summer 1202 – Spring 1203)

When the Crusaders mustered at the Lido in Venice in summer 1202, only a third of the expected troops arrived. Even after the French lords stripped their personal gold and silver plate, they were in default by 34,000 silver marks (Villehardouin, §§ 56–61).

Venice could not afford to write off 34,000 marks of silver; its entire merchant fleet and state capital were tied up in the vessels sitting in the lagoon.

Doge Enrico Dandolo, who also held the unpaid Byzantine indemnity claims of 1171/1198, offered a refinancing deal:

•Step 1: The Crusaders would work off the first part of their default by capturing the rival Christian Adriatic port of Zara (November 1202) for Venice.

•Step 2: At Zara, the exiled Byzantine Prince Alexios (IV) Angelos arrived, seeking military backing to overthrow his uncle (Alexios III) in Constantinople. In the Treaty of Zara (Spring 1203), Prince Alexios IV signed a sovereign promissory note: 

if the Venetian fleet and Crusader army placed him on the throne of Constantinople, the Byzantine Treasury would pay 200,000 marks of fine silver (immediately extinguishing the Crusaders' 34,000-mark debt to Venice and providing 166,000 marks in profit), plus a full year of provisions and 10,000 soldiers.

3. The Second Default and the Empty Treasury (July 1203 – February 1204)

In July 1203, the Venetian-Crusader force breached the Golden Horn and installed Alexios IV as co-emperor. Immediately, the bill came due AND Alexios IV discovered that a century of tax free Italian trade concessions and court corruption had left the Imperial Treasury virtually empty.

To pay the first 100,000 silver marks to the Venetians and Crusaders, Alexios IV was forced to:

•Impose emergency capital levies on the population of Constantinople;

•Confiscate the private wealth of his political opponents; and

•Physically strip the gold and silver lamps, chalices, and icons from the churches of Constantinople and melt them down at the mint (documented in horror by the Byzantine chronicler and eyewitness Niketas Choniates, Historia, pp. 551–552).

>>>>>> By late autumn 1203, after melting the church treasures, Alexios IV was still 100,000 silver marks short of his 200,000-mark obligation. When Doge Dandolo and the Crusader barons delivered an ultimatum demanding immediate payment in full, a popular anti-debt uprising inside Constantinople overthrew and strangled Alexios IV in January–February 1204, installing Alexios V Doukas ("Mourtzouphlos"), who formally repudiated the debt contract.

4. The Receivership Contract: The Pact of March 1204

The creditors did not walk away. They signed a formal Liquidation and Receivership Agreement outside the walls of Constantinople—the Pact of March 1204 (ASV, Pacta I; Tafel & Thomas, Vol. I, No. CXIX, pp. 444–452):

•The contract stipulated that the Venetian and Crusader forces would storm Constantinople and seize all movable wealth inside the city.

•From the plundered assets, Venice would receive the first 75 per cent of all proceeds until its entire 85,000 mark transport contract and all accrued Byzantine arrears were paid off in full.

•Under the accompanying Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae (Partition of the Lands of the Empire of Romania, October 1204) (ASV, Pacta, Liber Albus; Tafel & Thomas, Vol. I, No. CXXI),

••••••• the Byzantine Empire itself was carved up like a bankrupt corporation:

◦A Latin Emperor received one quarter (1/4) of the empire;

◦The Crusader barons received three eighths (3/8) as feudal fiefs and

◦The Republic of Venice received three eighths (3/8) of the entire Byzantine Empire, specifically selecting every strategic maritime choke point, island, and commercial port from the Ionian Sea and Crete to the Dardanelles (Gallipoli), the Sea of Marmara, and 3/8 of the city of Constantinople itself (Doge Dandolo adopting the formal title "Lord of One Quarter and One Half of One-Quarter of the Whole Roman Empire").

————————————

VI. SUMMARY OF PART 1: THE ARCHIVAL VERDICT ON 1082–1204

When Constantinople was stormed and looted for three days on 12–15 April 1204,

yielding an estimated 400,000 to 800,000 silver marks in plundered gold, silver, silk, and sacred relics (including the four bronze horses shipped to St. Mark’s Basilica in Venice), not a single Muslim soldier and not a single Jewish gatekeeper was involved.

The first destruction of the Byzantine Empire was an intra-Christian sovereign debt foreclosure:

1. The 1082 Chrysobull stripped the state of its 10% kommerkion customs revenue and handed wholesale trade to a tax-exempt Venetian syndicate.

2. The 1171–1198 Indemnity Treaties locked the state into sovereign debt arrears while Venice pioneered transferable state bonds (Imprestiti) to finance naval enforcement.

3. The 1201–1204 Debt Contracts turned a Crusader army into a private collection agency for 85,000 and then 200,000 Cologne marks of silver, culminating in the physical liquidation and partition of the empire when the Imperial Treasury could not pay.

Even when the Greek Palaiologos dynasty recaptured Constantinople in 1261, it did not regain an empire; it inherited a hollowed out shell.

The triangular shape is not an aesthetic choice. It is a geometric basin that minimizes the routing tax P_ent for electrostatic field propulsion. In MBU, thrust is not generated by pushing against air. It is generated by lowering the local sustainability threshold Theta in the direction of travel.

Electrostatic fields create a gradient in the transmissivity corridors T_ij of the surrounding lattice. By applying high voltage, the craft biases the alignment of nearby nodes. This creates a "cheap" path through the air. The craft does not fly; it slides down a slope of affordability that it creates for itself.

The silence is the key. Conventional engines create variance (Wiggle) in the form of sound and heat. This raises the routing tax for the surrounding environment. Electrostatic propulsion aligns the lattice without injecting chaotic noise. It is a smooth Sort event. The air molecules are not pushed; they are coerced into a coherent flow that offers zero resistance.

The Biefeld-Brown effect is the classical observation of this quantum geometric bias. The ion wind is just the visible residue of the lattice re-aligning to support the lock. The craft is essentially a mobile region of low-pressure geometry.

Why triangles? Because three points define a plane with maximum stability for minimal material cost. In lattice terms, a triangle is the simplest closed loop that can sustain a directed phase gradient. It allows the craft to maintain a stable Rung 4 lock while manipulating the local routing tax in three dimensions.

Rest in Lattice. Do not look for rockets. Look for the budget. And you will see that the triangle is just the most affordable way to cheat gravity.

#HarryPotter #HarryPotterfanfiction #HarryPotterworldbuilding

The Secretary of Magic and the Rogers Affair

The office of Secretary of Magic is, in formal terms, a cabinet position subject to the same political pressures and constraints as any other. In practice, the authority it confers has grown substantially as the United States expanded from a relatively insulated republic into the preeminent global power. This combination of institutional reach and limited public visibility has periodically attracted candidates whose ambitions or methods proved incompatible with the office.

The most serious case occurred in 1932 with the candidacy of Ezekiel Thomas Rogers. Rogers was of mixed German and Navajo ancestry. He publicly minimized the former while emphasizing a personal narrative of tragedy and self-advancement. His parents, a Navajo father and white mother, were killed on their Arizona farm by a group of Navajo who objected to the couple’s experimentation with Dark Arts—specifically, attempts to combine Aztec blood-magic techniques with contemporary non-magical medical knowledge. Orphaned, Rogers attended Plotinus Academy on scholarship, enlisted in the United States Mage Corps, and was promoted from sergeant to lieutenant for actions against German mages in the First World War. He received the Franklin Star for valor. Throughout this period he continued private research into the Dark Arts his parents had pursued. After the war he obtained papers from an abandoned French magical residence concerning advanced Aztec and Navajo blood practices. He later joined the faculty of the Salem School of Witchcraft as a professor of Ancient Magic Rituals. His 1925 doctoral thesis on a blood-replenishment ritual earned the Galen Prize for Magical Medicine; the work was, in fact, a reconstruction of Aztec rites whose origins he did not disclose.

Around 1930 Rogers completed the Skinwalker transformation. He survived the process by means of Aztec blood-replenishment rituals. Three of the Navajo men responsible for his parents’ deaths did not. Thereafter he required periodic human sacrifices to stabilize his altered state. While cultivating political alliances and standing as a candidate for Secretary of Magic—with the public support of Franklin D. Roosevelt—he grew less able to conceal the physical and mental costs of the transformation.

The disappearance of a young woman last seen in Rogers’s company drew the attention of Freeman Savage, a private investigator and fellow veteran of the First World War. Savage interrupted an attempted sacrifice, extracted the intended victim, and escaped. Rogers responded by having Savage declared a kidnapper and murderer and dispatching Aurors in pursuit. Savage evaded capture, entered the MACUSA building, and, employing a Navajo spell and totem supplied by an associate, revealed Rogers’s nature before the assembled Magical Congress. Rogers resisted; concentrated spellfire together with machine-gun and grenade fire brought him down.

Savage was subsequently recognized as a national hero. President Roosevelt awarded him the Presidential Medal of Freedom and offered him the post of Secretary of Magic. Savage declined the office but accepted substantial compensation for the resolution of the case. The position then passed to Jonathan Akroyd, a wizard of established reputation who held it through the Second World War.

Savage had many more adventures before, during and after the Second World War... But that's another story.
